propositions: A dirty tracker must be staged, committed with supplied or ambient git identity, and then pushed without nested locks; committed content must survive delivery to origin.
A clean but locally-ahead tracker must push without creating an empty commit; under strict mode, persistent rejection must raise dependency-defined PushDeliveryError and preserve the local commit.

An active rebase or merge-recovery state must block the commit phase before staging: strict mode raises merge-recovery-blocked reason, default mode logs warning and returns with dirty content intact for later retry.

Lock, staging, and commit failures under strict mode must raise the exact dependency-defined PushDeliveryError with stable reasons (commit-lock-timeout, stage-failed, commit-failed); default mode must warn, return without pushing, and retain uncommitted content for clean retry.
Supplied git user identity (name/email) must appear in commit author metadata; omitted identity must use ambient repository identity; global or repository config must never be mutated.
Direct push_tickets_branch must remain push-only without staging or committing dirty trees; new commit_and_push_tickets_branch must not weaken existing push-only callers or vocabulary.
